The Viet Cong military structure in South Vietnam is standardised, with three types of soldiers. Village-based guerrillas typically work during the day and are available for assignments at night or in emergencies. In areas under VC control, a squad of 10 to 16 men is common, often equipped with land mines, rifles, or submachine guns. At the district level, half-time irregular forces are organised into companies of 50 or more men, who receive partial pay and are better equipped and trained than village-level units. Many recruits are coerced through kidnapping, threats, or familial pressure, rather than volunteering.

A quick fire plan is typically developed at the brigade level or lower and is created directly between the artillery officer and the commander of the supported arm. It is used for rapid deployment of artillery support, often for an imminent attack within an hour, and involves a limited number of targets and batteries. It is distinct from a deliberate fire plan, which is usually initiated at a higher level and involves the coordinated fire of multiple regiments.
